newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel shares advance on broker upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel shares advance on broker upgrades.

text.p: SBC-Warburg and SGE Delahaye have upgraded their recommendations on French engineering group Alcatel Alsthom, a day after chairman Serge Tchuruk's 1996 results presentation, fund managers said on Wednesday.
SBC-Warburg has gone to short-term buy from hold, while SGE Delahaye has marked the stock up to outperform from neutral.
Alcatel shares were up 2.25 percent at 682 francs at 1550 GMT on volume of 1.4 million shares.
One fund manager said all brokers, except Goldman Sachs, rated the stock a buy.
Morgan Stanley, which rates Alcatel a strong buy with a target of 750 francs, has put the stock on its international focus list.

SBC Warburg, citing a higher than expected 1996 dividend and larger debt repayment than initially announced, pointed to the optimistic tone of Tuesday's analysts' meeting and a bounce in telecommunications orders in the fourth quarter. The broker concluded that "the worst is over".
But certain worries remain, such as uncertainty over the cashflow composition, significant goodwill on the balance sheet and the renewed offer for Thomson-CSF.
These led the broker to rate the share a short-term buy.

SGE Delahaye, which has been neutral on the stock for a long time, noted the 1996 results were better than expected and the group showed a "very combative" spirit in telecommunications. It said the stock had potential to go to 760/770 francs.
